method: Agent-enumerated from domain knowledge cross-checked against events/*.yaml and candidate_triggers/*.yaml. Each candidate verified via WebSearch against contemporaneous reporting and, where available, primary DOJ/SEC/CFTC/FinCEN/foreign-regulator pages. No automated scraper used.
cross_check_method: Each candidate slug cross-checked against the 109 admitted event ids and the 21 promoted_event_id values in candidate_triggers/. Verified events already in corpus for this tier: china-pboc-crypto-ban-2013-12, silk-road-doj-seizure-2013, sec-shavers-btcst-2013, shrem-faiella-bitcoin-exchange-2014, powell-unlicensed-bitcoin-exchange-2014, sec-voorhees-satoshidice-2014, sec-burnside-bitcoin-stock-exchange-2014, nydfs-bitlicense-2015-06, ripple-fincen-xrp-2015, coinflip-cftc-derivabit-2015, teraexchange-cftc-bitcoin-swap-2015, bitfinex-cftc-retail-commodity-2016, coinbase-irs-john-doe-summons-2016.
exclusion_notes: Liberty Reserve 2013-05 was previously screened out as 'rejected_out_of_scope: non-blockchain digital-currency precursor' per sources/source_frame_triage/us_federal_enforcement_archives.csv. Retained here as P2/deferred for parity (Liberty Reserve was the dominant non-bitcoin digital-currency takedown of 2013, frequently cited as a contextual precursor to the FinCEN MSB regime that followed).
BTC-e seizure / Vinnik arrest is 2017-07 and is already coded as btc-e-doj-2017; outside the historical_baseline_2013_2016 scope window. Not enumerated.
AlphaBay/Hansa darknet takedowns are 2017-07; already coded as alphabay-hansa-doj-2017. Not enumerated.

Mt. Gox creditor proceedings continue through 2014-present; the 2014-02-28 civil rehabilitation filing in Tokyo District Court is enumerated here as a single bankruptcy-court-mediated event. The 2014-04-16 conversion to bankruptcy + the 2014-11-26 Tibanne (parent) bankruptcy filing are noted in the bankruptcy candidate's rationale but not re-enumerated as separate candidates.
USMS Silk Road bitcoin auctions (Jun 2014, Dec 2014, Mar 2015, Nov 2015) are administrative disposal of seized assets, not censorship events; not enumerated as separate candidates.

Ross Ulbricht arrest 2013-10-01 is enumerated as a candidate separate from silk-road-doj-seizure-2013 (which covers the Oct-02 / Oct-25 BTC seizures) only because the arrest itself is the load-bearing operator-takedown trigger; if existing silk-road-doj-seizure-2013 already covers the arrest scope, this candidate should be folded in rather than admitted.

Vietnam SBV 2014 has no clean primary-source SBV publication for that year; the explicit SBV prohibition document is Official Letter 5747/NHNN-PC dated July 2017, outside this tier. Marked P2 / deferred.
UK HMRC Brief 09/14 (March 2014) is tax classification (bitcoin = VAT-exempt currency-equivalent) rather than a censorship/access action; included as P2 because cascade observability is weak.

candidates.title: DHS/IRS seizure of Mt. Gox Dwolla and Wells Fargo accounts (Mutum Sigillum)
candidates.rationale: First major US federal action against a bitcoin exchange. DHS/HSI seizure warrant signed by Magistrate Judge Susan K. Gauvey (D. Md.) on 2013-05-14 against Mutum Sigillum LLC's Dwolla account at Veridian Credit Union; second warrant against Wells Fargo account 2013-05-09. Total $5M seized May-Aug 2013 ($2.9M Dwolla + $2.1M Wells Fargo). Predicate: Mt. Gox subsidiary operating as unregistered MSB in violation of 18 USC 1960. Direct cascade: triggered Mt. Gox USD-withdrawal suspension 2013-06-20 and the chain of bank defenstrations leading to bankruptcy. Cleanest 2013 federal off-ramp-cex cascade trigger; foundational precedent for the entire FinCEN-MSB-enforcement era. Primary court documents (warrants) are scanned; need to source from PACER for the body_hash, but contemporaneous TechCrunch/CoinDesk/Slashdot reporting is dense and consistent.

candidates.title: Mt. Gox civil rehabilitation / bankruptcy filing (Tokyo District Court)
candidates.rationale: Largest crypto-exchange collapse of the tier; 850,000 BTC (~7% of supply) lost. Civil rehabilitation filed 2014-02-28 in Tokyo District Court (Case 2014 (fu) No. 3830); converted to bankruptcy 2014-04-16; parent Tibanne filed bankruptcy 2014-11-26. The bankruptcy trustee proceedings remain the single most-cited 2013-2016 cross-border insolvency in crypto. Cascade observable: BTC/USD halved within 6 weeks, all customer USD/BTC withdrawals frozen permanently, Japanese banking system de-risked further from bitcoin. Court documents available via mtgox.com archive and Tokyo District Court records; primary citation needs court-bulletin replay.

candidates.title: DOJ SDNY indictment of Anthony Murgio and Yuri Lebedev (Coin.MX)
candidates.rationale: Major SDNY post-Shrem unlicensed-exchange indictment. Coin.MX operated 2013-2015 processing >$10M, fronted by phony 'Collectors Club' and used a captured federal credit union (HOPE FCU, NJ) for banking. Murgio sentenced 5.5 years (Jun 2017). Distinct from shrem-faiella-bitcoin-exchange-2014 (same DOJ stratum but different operators, different conduit, different fraud scheme — Coin.MX added ransomware-cashout angle and credit-union takeover). Cleanest 2015 federal unlicensed-MSB cascade; ties to the JPMorgan/E*Trade hack indictments unsealed same day.

candidates.title: FinCEN guidance FIN-2013-G001 on virtual currency administrators and exchangers as MSBs
candidates.rationale: Foundational US regulatory frame for the entire 2013-2016 tier. FIN-2013-G001 (2013-03-18) declared that administrators and exchangers of convertible virtual currency are money transmitters subject to BSA registration, reporting, and recordkeeping; users are not. Cited as the predicate for nearly every subsequent US bitcoin enforcement (Mt. Gox Dwolla seizure, Shrem-Faiella, Powell, Coin.MX, Ripple, BTC-e). Class-level guidance with no concrete target — but the source_frame_triage previously screened similar policy-class rows as 'screened_no_extractor_target'. Included here as P0 because schema admits policy_class triggers with observable downstream-cascade evidence (e.g., voluntary MSB registrations Apr-Dec 2013 documented in FinCEN MSB lookup).

candidates.title: NYDFS BitLicense compliance deadline cascade (Bitfinex/Kraken/ShapeShift/Poloniex NY exit)
candidates.rationale: L4-frontend cascade of NY-state geofencing across at least 10 platforms: Bitfinex (2015-08-15 withdrawal cutoff), Kraken (2015-08-09 exit, CEO Powell statement), ShapeShift (2015-06-11 exit, CEO Voorhees statement), Poloniex, BitQuick, BTCGuild, Eobot, Genesis Mining, GoCoin, LocalBitcoins, Paxful. Triggered by 2015-08-10 expiration of 45-day BitLicense grace period after the 2015-06-24 nydfs-bitlicense-2015-06 (already in corpus) regulation went into effect 2015-07-24. Distinct from nydfs-bitlicense-2015-06 because that event codes the rulemaking; this event codes the platform-exit cascade. Cleanest 2015 US-state-level offramp_cex + l4_frontend cascade.

candidates.title: SEC v. Homero Joshua Garza, GAW Miners, ZenMiner (cloud-mining securities fraud)
candidates.rationale: Major SEC bitcoin-mining securities action filed 2015-12-01 in D. Conn. (15-cv-01760). $20M Hashlet pseudo-mining contract sold Aug-Dec 2014 to >10,000 investors; SEC alleged GAW lacked computing power for promised mining. $11M default judgment Jun 2017; Garza separately pleaded guilty to wire fraud and sentenced 21 months. Distinct from sec-shavers-btcst-2013 (Ponzi) and sec-voorhees-satoshidice-2014 (unregistered share offering) — Garza is the cloud-mining-as-security doctrine case. Cleanest 2015 SEC asset_onchain + offramp_cex cascade.

candidates.title: Ross Ulbricht arrest, FBI San Francisco (Silk Road operator takedown)
candidates.rationale: Operator-arrest leg of the Silk Road takedown distinct from the asset-seizure leg coded as silk-road-doj-seizure-2013 (which covers 2013-10-02 / 2013-10-25 BTC seizures). Arrest at Glen Park library 2013-10-01 by FBI/IRS-CI/HSI. Initial BTC seizure 26,000; rolled up to 144,336 BTC after laptop forensics. Conviction Feb 2015, life sentence May 2015. P0 if treated as a distinct trigger; if existing silk-road-doj-seizure-2013 already includes the arrest under its scope, fold this into the parent rather than admit. Verify before promotion.

candidates.title: Bank of Thailand bitcoin trading prohibition (July 2013) and silent reversal (February 2014)
candidates.rationale: First nation-state bitcoin trading prohibition. 2013-07-29: BoT Foreign Exchange Administration Department informed Bitcoin Co Ltd that buying/selling, sending in/out of Thailand, and using for goods/services was illegal absent capital-control approval. Bitcoin Co Ltd suspended trading. Silently lifted 2014-02-15. Primary BoT publication is not archived on the public BoT site; the de-facto record is the Bitcoin Co Ltd statement reproduced by Asian Correspondent and CoinDesk. needs_check because the BoT statement itself was a meeting communication, not a published gazette notice. Useful as the first comparable_main precedent for the China 2013-12 PBoC notice and the 2014 wave (Russia, Indonesia, Vietnam, Bangladesh, Bolivia, Iceland).

candidates.title: Banco Central de Bolivia Resolution Directorate No. 044/2014 prohibiting bitcoin and altcoins
candidates.rationale: First explicit nation-state crypto-asset prohibition by central-bank resolution. BCB Resolutivo del Directorio No. 044/2014 of 2014-05-06 prohibited use of any currency or denomination not issued or regulated by Bolivia, naming Bitcoin, Namecoin, Tonal, Litecoin, Peercoin, Quark, Primecoin, Feathercoin. Lifted Jun 2024 by Resolution 082/2024. Primary URL inferred from BCB public-document path pattern; needs_check to pin the exact PDF URL. The 10-year duration makes this the longest continuous nation-state crypto ban in the tier.

candidates.title: Bangladesh Bank press release warning against bitcoin transactions
candidates.rationale: Bangladesh Bank press release citing Foreign Exchange Regulation Act 1947 + Money Laundering Prevention Act 2012; international press reported as 'criminalization' with up to 12-year sentence, though legal scholars dispute the criminalization framing (no statutory notification defining bitcoin as currency). Useful comparable_main for the 2014 nation-state warning wave. Primary BB press release URL on bb.org.bd is no longer reachable at original path; secondary citation chain is consistent. needs_check to pin BB archive snapshot.

candidates.title: Central Bank of Iceland statement: bitcoin trading restricted by Foreign Exchange Act
candidates.rationale: CBI 2014-03-19 statement: bitcoin foreign-exchange trading prohibited under Icelandic Foreign Exchange Act capital-controls regime (legacy of 2008 banking crisis). De-facto bitcoin ban via FX-control mechanism. Lifted 2017 with capital-control easing. Useful as a 'collateral censorship via FX controls' precedent (mechanism distinct from explicit crypto-ban). CBI primary URL verified.

candidates.title: Central Bank of Russia information letter on virtual currencies / Bitcoin (monetary surrogate prohibition)
candidates.rationale: CBR information letter 'On Using Virtual Currencies, Specifically Bitcoin, in Transactions' 2014-01-27; warned that bitcoin distribution may violate Article 27 of the Federal Law on the Central Bank prohibiting monetary surrogates. Followed by Prosecutor General Office statement Feb 2014 declaring crypto use a violation. First Russian-state position; predicate for the subsequent 2014-2022 cycle of bills. Library of Congress page is a research-quality primary-equivalent citation; CBR original Russian-language publication URL on cbr.ru should replace it during admission.

candidates.title: Bank Indonesia press release: Bitcoin and virtual currencies are not legal payment instruments
candidates.rationale: BI first public warning 2014-02-06 (some secondary sources cite 2014-01-16 as the soft warning, formalized 2014-02-06). Stance later hardened into 2017 ban on bitcoin as a payment instrument and 2019 Bappebti commodity-classification regime. Primary URL on bi.go.id is an old WordPress-style path that may no longer resolve; needs_check to pin BI press-release archive snapshot.

candidates.title: Argentina UIF Resolution 300/2014 requiring bitcoin transaction reporting by obligated entities
candidates.rationale: Argentina UIF (FIU) Resolution 300/2014: first Latin American AML reporting regime explicitly naming virtual currencies. Required obligated entities to report all client transactions involving 'monedas virtuales'. Predicate for the later AFIP tax-reporting regime (2015-2017) and the 2024 CNV crypto-VASP registration regime. InfoLEG URL pattern is canonical for Argentine norma publication; needs_check to confirm the exact 'norma.htm' anchor.

candidates.title: Banco Central do Brasil Comunicado nº 25.306 warning on virtual / encrypted currency risks
candidates.rationale: BCB Comunicado 25.306 of 2014-02-19: first BR central-bank statement on bitcoin / 'moedas virtuais'. Warning-class (not prohibition). Predicate for 2017 Comunicado 31.379 and 2022 Marco Legal das Criptomoedas (Law 14.478/2022). Primary URL inferred from BCB normativo search pattern; needs_check to pin direct PDF anchor.

candidates.title: EBA Opinion on Virtual Currencies EBA/Op/2014/08 (national supervisors should discourage credit/payment/e-money institutions from VC activity)
candidates.rationale: EBA/Op/2014/08 of 2014-07-04: identified 70+ risks of virtual currencies; recommended that national supervisors discourage credit, payment, and e-money institutions from buying/holding/selling VCs pending a comprehensive regulatory regime. Foundational European supranational-stratum document; predecessor to 5AMLD (2018), MiCA (2023, already coded). Direct cascade observable: multiple EU member-state banks subsequently de-banked bitcoin exchanges through 2014-2017.

candidates.title: FATF Report 'Virtual Currencies: Key Definitions and Potential AML/CFT Risks' (June 2014)
candidates.rationale: FATF June 2014 report: first FATF-stratum document on virtual currencies; established the ML/TF risk taxonomy that became the 2015 Risk-Based Approach guidance and ultimately Recommendation 15 / Travel Rule (already coded as fatf-r15-vasp-travel-rule-2019). Predicate for the entire global VASP-licensing wave. Pairs with eba-virtual-currencies-opinion as the two foundational 2014 supranational frame-setters.

candidates.title: CoinLab v. Mt. Gox civil breach-of-contract suit (W.D. Wash.)
candidates.rationale: CoinLab v. Mt. Gox 2:13-cv-00777 (W.D. Wash., filed 2013-05-02): $75M breach-of-contract suit (Mt. Gox failed to give CoinLab exclusive NA bitcoin-exchange rights under Nov 2012 agreement). Mt. Gox countersued $5.5M (2013-09). CoinLab claim later inflated to $16B in Mt. Gox bankruptcy proceedings, freezing creditor distribution for years. Codes a US-civil-litigation track for the Mt. Gox cascade distinct from the federal-enforcement track (mtgox-dhs-dwolla-wells-fargo-seizure-2013) and the Japanese-bankruptcy track (mtgox-bankruptcy-tokyo-2014). PACER docket is canonical primary.

candidates.title: Mt. Gox suspension of USD withdrawals (operator action triggered by US banking constraints)
candidates.rationale: 2013-06-20 Mt. Gox press release announcing 2-week USD-withdrawal suspension. Caused directly by Mizuho Bank's mid-2013 refusal to process international wire transfers (which was itself triggered by the May DHS Dwolla/Wells Fargo seizure warrants). First major operator-driven cascade event of the tier; cleanest example of a federal-action -> banking-derisking -> operator-withdrawal-freeze chain. S0_operator_action stratum (if defined) or admit as a derived event from mtgox-dhs-dwolla-wells-fargo-seizure-2013.

candidates.title: Mark Karpelès arrest by Tokyo Metropolitan Police Department (Mt. Gox operator)
candidates.rationale: Mark Karpelès arrested 2015-08-01 by Tokyo MPD on data-manipulation charges; re-arrested Nov 2015 on embezzlement; indicted Sep 2015. Convicted Mar 2019 on one count of data manipulation (30 months suspended), acquitted of embezzlement / breach of trust. First criminal action against a major-exchange operator in Japan; operator-takedown leg of the Mt. Gox cascade distinct from the bankruptcy and the US civil/federal tracks. Primary citation needs Japanese court / National Police Agency source; secondary sources are dense.

candidates.title: Cryptsy exchange collapse + CFTC/SEC class action (Vernon flight to China)
candidates.rationale: Cryptsy (founded May 2013, Florida) ceased operations 2016-01-13 citing alleged Jul-2014 hack of cold-storage BTC. Founder Paul 'Big Vern' Vernon fled to China 2015. SD Fla. class action 2016-04 secured $8.2M judgment. Subsequent DOJ indictment 2019 (unsealed Jan 2022) on wire fraud / tax evasion. Pre-DOJ-indictment phase (within tier): operator-takedown cascade documented via private civil litigation in S. Fla. Useful as the cleanest 2016 operator-collapse case alongside the Bitfinex hack.

candidates.title: The DAO exploit + Ethereum hard fork (community-mediated state rollback)
candidates.rationale: 2016-06-17: DAO reentrancy exploit drains 3.6M ETH (~$70M). 2016-07-20: Ethereum block 1,920,000 hard fork rolls back the drain, creating ETH (post-fork) and ETC (pre-fork). 2017-07-25: SEC Report of Investigation Pursuant to §21(a) holds DAO tokens are securities (a class-level enforcement-equivalent action). Within tier: only the 2016 hard fork. Codes the first major L1-consensus-layer rollback event triggered by a smart-contract exploit — directly relevant to the L1 censorship layer. Distinct because the censorship action is by Ethereum protocol developers (operators), not a state actor.

candidates.title: Bitfinex 2016-08 hack (119,756 BTC stolen) + retroactive socialized-loss BFX token issuance
candidates.rationale: 2016-08-02: 119,756 BTC stolen from Bitfinex multisig in ~3 hours due to BitGo-key configuration error. Bitfinex socialized losses across all customers (~36% haircut) and issued BFX tokens. Lichtenstein pleaded guilty Aug 2023 to the theft; Morgan ('Razzlekhan') guilty Aug 2023. Within tier: only the hack itself and the immediate socialized-loss / BFX issuance. Codes the largest 2016 exchange compromise and the first known instance of forced bail-in cascading onto customer balances. Cleanest 2016 offramp_cex + asset_onchain cascade trigger.

candidates.title: HMRC Revenue & Customs Brief 09/14: bitcoin treated as currency for VAT purposes
candidates.rationale: HMRC R&C Brief 09/14 (2014-03-03): bitcoin mining outside VAT scope; bitcoin/sterling exchanges VAT-exempt as currency-equivalent. Tax-classification action, not censorship/access action — cascade observability is weak. Useful only as a 'comparable_baseline' UK datapoint within the broader 2014 EU/G20 frame-setting wave. P2: include only if the schema admits tax-classification triggers; otherwise screen out.

candidates.title: Liberty Reserve DOJ takedown (Budovsky indictment SDNY)
candidates.rationale: Liberty Reserve indictment unsealed 2013-05-28: $6B money-laundering scheme, 5.5M users, first major application of Patriot Act §311 to a digital-currency platform. PREVIOUSLY SCREENED OUT in sources/source_frame_triage/us_federal_enforcement_archives.csv as 'rejected_out_of_scope: non-blockchain digital-currency precursor retained as screened context not comparable crypto target' (decision 2026-05-16). Retained here as P2/deferred because: (a) it is the cleanest 2013 precedent for the 18 USC 1960 / 311 / forfeiture playbook later applied to BTC-e (2017) and Bitzlato (2023); (b) the Wikipedia/InsightCrime literature consistently lists it as the predicate event for crypto-exchange enforcement even though Liberty Reserve itself was not bitcoin. RECOMMEND: maintain screen-out unless the dataset accepts a 'precursor_context' admission tier.

candidates.title: State Bank of Vietnam press statement: bitcoin not recognized as currency / payment instrument
candidates.rationale: Secondary sources reference an SBV press statement in early 2014 declaring bitcoin not a legal payment instrument under Vietnamese law, but the explicit SBV prohibition document is Official Letter 5747/NHNN-PC dated 2017-07, OUTSIDE this tier. No clean 2014 primary URL on sbv.gov.vn was located. P2 / deferred until a 2014 SBV publication is located; otherwise screen out and admit only the 2017 Official Letter under the comparable_main tier.
